title: Regiment and Harbor
premise: In the port town of Vellamare, on the eve of a revolution nobody believes will arrive, Oscar Nakamura works in his late father's print shop, cutting type and keeping the town's civic ledger — the book that records every name, debt, and birth. When the royal army requisitions the harbor and demands the ledger to compile lists of conscripts and 'disloyals,' Oscar must choose between surrendering the names of his neighbors or forging a new book while the soldiers occupy the streets above his cellar workshop. Over ten days, as the requisition ship waits on the tide, he finishes the true ledger in secret with help from the harbormaster's widow and a deserter who once arrested his father. The novel ends at dawn: Oscar hands the army a forged ledger, smuggles the real one aboard a fishing boat bound for exile, and stays behind — inheriting not his father's trade alone, but the burden of being the one who remembers.
about_author: Orsen Halloran is the pen name of a former letterpress compositor who spent fifteen years restoring printing equipment in coastal museum workshops before turning to fiction. He writes historical novels about ordinary tradespeople caught inside large machinery of state, and lives within sight of a working harbor.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Letters
chapters.summary: Oscar Nakamura's POV. In the Nakamura print shop, Oscar cuts replacement sorts for the town ledger his father kept until his death, insisting history happens elsewhere. A routine day of invoices, gossip, and the harbormaster's widow collecting notices establishes the town's rhythms. Emotional beat: quiet grief disguised as competence; Oscar believes invisibility is safety.

chapters.title: Gunpowder Smell at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Warships appear off the point; an advance officer requisitions the harbor, the granary, and — with bureaucratic courtesy — all civic records, including the ledger of names. The town council defers; fear spreads through the market. Emotional beat: the first crack in Oscar's belief that distance protects him; the ledger is suddenly a weapon he is holding.

chapters.title: Requisition
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV, with a brief interlude from Captain Aldous Reyne, the courteous occupation commander. Soldiers billet in the square; Reyne gives Oscar three days to deliver the ledger before it ships on the morning tide. Oscar hides the original beneath the type cases and begins copying pages to buy time. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Names Are Not Neutral
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Studying the ledger to plan the forgery, Oscar confronts what his father recorded: debts forgiven quietly, a birth entered under the wrong name, the deserter Tomas Ferro listed as dead years ago. Each entry is a small mercy or a small betrayal. Emotional beat: inheritance revealed as moral weight, not just property.

chapters.title: The Widow's Hand
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Oscar and Maren Ostervik, the harbormaster's widow. Maren catches Oscar forging entries and, instead of denouncing him, reveals she can forge a clerk's hand better than he can — her husband taught her. They form an uneasy alliance. Emotional beat: belonging found in complicity; two loners becoming conspirators.

chapters.title: A Deserter in the Cellar
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Tomas Ferro — alive, hunted, once the soldier who escorted Oscar's father to prison — takes refuge in the print shop cellar. Oscar must decide whether hatred or usefulness governs. Ferro knows what the army does with ledgers: last town's list became a firing squad roster. Emotional beat: loyalty tested against truth; forgiveness begins as arithmetic.

chapters.title: What the Tide Takes
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. The requisition ship anchors in the harbor; Reyne grows suspicious of delays and searches half the town. Maren arranges passage on her late husband's fishing boat, but only if the true ledger leaves before dawn. She sacrifices her chance to sail with it. Emotional beat: love expressed as logistics; the cost of staying made concrete.

chapters.title: Three Days, Two Books
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The forgery nears completion, but Reyne demands the ledger a day early after a raid uncovers pamphlets printed on Nakamura stock. Oscar must finish the true ledger — every name corrected, every mercy preserved — overnight while soldiers patrol above the cellar. Emotional beat: craft as resistance; exhaustion transfigured into purpose.

chapters.title: The Morning of Names
chapters.summary: Climax, Oscar's POV. At the dockside handover, Reyne leafs through the forged ledger as the fishing boat slips its moorings behind him. A soldier spots the sail; Ferro creates a diversion and is taken. Reyne, suspecting but unable to prove the deception, lets Oscar go — 'books outlive officers.' Emotional beat: triumph laced with unbearable cost.

chapters.title: Regiment and Harbor
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV, epilogue weeks later. The regiment marches out; the town rebuilds around absences. Oscar reopens the shop, hangs his father's cutting tools beside his own, and begins a new ledger in his own hand — knowing the old one sails toward exile and survival. Emotional beat: acceptance of inheritance; invisibility renounced, memory chosen as vocation.
